heard: The coldest atmosphere isn't on the planet farthest away. Uranus hits minus 371 degrees Fahrenheit, even though Neptune is farther. Methane gas absorbs red light, turning the world blue-green. A giant collision likely knocked the entire planet sideways. This ice giant orbits on its side every 84 years. NASA's Voyager 2 swept past this frozen giant in 1986. Voyager found its magnetic center offset by a third of its radius. It holds the record for the solar system's coldest atmosphere.
